definitions.explanation: Something that is not final or permanent but serves as a placeholder or stopgap until a proper arrangement is made.
Used to indicate a hypothetical situation or assumption, often in the pattern {仮|かり}に〜としても.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}の{名前|なまえ}をつけた。
examples.english: I gave it a tentative name.

examples.japanese: まだ{仮|かり}の{予定|よてい}なので、{変更|へんこう}になるかもしれません。
examples.english: It's still a tentative schedule, so it may change.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}の{住|す}まいで{半年|はんとし}{暮|く}らした。
examples.english: I lived in temporary housing for half a year.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}にそうだとしても、{問題|もんだい}はない。
examples.english: Even supposing that were the case, there would be no problem.

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}に{彼|かれ}が{来|こ}なかったら、どうする？
examples.english: Hypothetically, if he doesn't come, what will we do?

examples.japanese: {仮|かり}に{百万円|ひゃくまんえん}あったとしても、この{家|いえ}は{買|か}えない。
examples.english: Even if you hypothetically had one million yen, you couldn't buy this house.

notes:
Modifies nouns directly as {仮|かり}の〜 (temporary ~). In sense 2, used adverbially as {仮|かり}に at the start of a sentence to introduce a hypothesis. The kanji {仮|かり} also appears in many compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仮|かり}の{姿|すがた} (disguised form, temporary appearance)
- {仮|かり}{住|ず}まい (temporary dwelling)
- {仮|かり}{免許|めんきょ} (provisional license, learner's permit)
- {仮|かり}{設定|せってい} (tentative setting)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仮|かり}に〜としても (even supposing that ~)
- {仮|かり}に〜たら (hypothetically, if ~)
